title: Sprint 5 - Sorting, Limiting & Updating
description: Complete all MongoDB queries in this sprint.

tickets.title: Sort Tasks Ascending
tickets.description:
Get the `_id` and `title` of all tasks, ordered by priority in ascending order.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
SELECT id, title FROM todos ORDER BY priority ASC;
```
tasks: Get the `_id` and `title` of all tasks, ordered by priority in ascending order.
hints: Chain .sort({ priority: 1 }) onto your find() query.

tickets.title: Top 5 Recent Tasks (DESC)
tickets.description:
Get the 5 most recently created todos (assuming highest `_id` is most recent). Fetch their `_id` and `title`.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
SELECT id, title FROM todos ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;
```
tasks: Get the 5 most recently created todos (assuming highest `_id` is most recent). Fetch their `_id` and `title`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting descending sort (-1) or wrong limit.

tickets.title: Complete a Task
tickets.description:
Task with `_id = 1` has been finished. Change its status to 'completed'.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
UPDATE todos SET status = 'completed' WHERE id = 1;
```
tasks: Task with `_id = 1` has been finished. Change its status to 'completed'.
learning_objectives: Update a single document using updateOne.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the $set operator or omitting the filter.

tickets.title: Delete Old Data
tickets.description:
Delete any todos that belong to `user_id = 2`.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
DELETE FROM todos WHERE user_id = 2;
```
tasks: Delete any todos that belong to `user_id = 2`.

tickets.title: Increment Priority
tickets.description:
Increase the `priority` of all pending todos by 1.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
UPDATE todos SET priority = priority + 1 WHERE status = 'pending';
```
tasks: Increase the `priority` of all pending todos by 1.
common_mistakes: Using $set instead of $inc, or forgetting update filter.
hints: Use updateMany with { status: "pending" } and $inc operator.

tickets.title: Unset a Field ($unset)
tickets.description:
Remove the `due_date` field entirely from all documents in the `todos` collection.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
ALTER TABLE todos DROP COLUMN due_date;
```
tasks: Remove the `due_date` field entirely from all documents in the `todos` collection.
learning_objectives: Remove a field from documents using $unset.
common_mistakes: Using $set to set it to null instead of completely removing it via $unset.

tickets.title: Rename a Field ($rename)
tickets.description:
Rename the `title` field to `task_name` in all documents of the `todos` collection.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
ALTER TABLE todos RENAME COLUMN title TO task_name;
```
tasks: Rename the `title` field to `task_name` in all documents of the `todos` collection.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to quote field names inside the $rename block.

tickets.title: Replace a Document Entirely (replaceOne)
tickets.description:
Replace user with `_id = 2` (Bob) with a new profile having the username 'Robert' and no other user-defined fields (such as email). Note: In MongoDB, `replaceOne()` completely replaces all user-defined fields of the target document, but the `_id` field is automatically preserved and remains unchanged.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
UPDATE users SET username = 'Robert', email = NULL WHERE id = 2;
```
tasks: Replace user with `_id = 2` (Bob) with a new profile having the username 'Robert' and no other user-defined fields (such as email). Note: In MongoDB, `replaceOne()` completely replaces all user-defined fields of the target document, but the `_id` field is automatically preserved and remains unchanged.
learning_objectives: Learn replaceOne and understand the preservation of _id.
common_mistakes: Trying to include _id in the replacement object (causes write error) or using updateOne with $set.
